original_question: For the hard instances of the minimum r-cover problem on continuous graphs, namely when r is a non-unit fraction, what lower bounds on approximation hardness can be proved for computing the minimum number of radius-r balls needed to cover the graph?
target_in_paper: Section 3.2 ("Vertex cover"), subsection "(In)approximability," final open question: "For the hard cases of the problem (with the radius r being a non-unit fraction, see Hartmann et al [9]), what are the lower bounds for the inapproximability of the minimum r-cover problem?"

A radius-r ball is defined in this metric space, and an r-cover is a family of such balls whose union covers every point of G.
The centers of the balls are allowed to lie anywhere in the continuous graph G, not just at the endpoints V.
The objective quantity should be named explicitly: tau_r(G), the minimum cardinality of an r-cover of G.

In the nearby context, the hard regime is specifically rational radii r > 0 that are non-unit fractions; the paper first notes that for every rational r the problem is in NP, then recalls Hartmann et al.'s result that unit fractions are polynomial-time solvable while non-unit fractions are NP-hard.

The approximation question is about polynomial-time inapproximability bounds, i.e. lower bounds on achievable approximation ratios, rather than exact complexity or existence of approximation algorithms.
The usual complexity qualifier underlying such a question (for example, unless P = NP) is implicit in the draft and should be made explicit in a stand-alone formulation.
No ambient ring, field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency conditions are relevant here; the hidden assumptions are entirely those of the metric-graph model.
refined_question: Let G be a continuous graph in the sense of the paper: a metric graph obtained from a finite endpoint set with each edge realized as a unit-length continuous interval, and with distance given by the shortest-path metric on all points of G. For a rational radius r > 0, let tau_r(G) denote the minimum number of radius-r balls, with centers allowed anywhere in G, whose union covers all points of G. Hartmann et al. are cited as showing that this minimum r-cover problem is polynomial-time solvable when r is a unit fraction and NP-hard when r is a non-unit fraction. For the hard regime—namely, rational radii r that are non-unit fractions (not of the form 1/q with q in N)—what lower bounds can be proved on the polynomial-time approximability of tau_r(G), i.e. which approximation ratios can be ruled out for the minimum r-cover problem on general continuous graphs unless P = NP?
